# Owner REST Endpoints via OfficeFloor Function Injection

The app is spring-petclinic reimplemented on OfficeFloor. Each REST endpoint is a YAML file naming a chain of Java "function" classes wired via `next:`; each function class exposes one `service(...)` method whose parameters are dependency-injected (repositories, mappers, `@Val` published objects, `@RequestBody`, `@PathVariable`, `ObjectResponse`, `Out<T>`). Escalations (checked exceptions) map to HTTP responses via handler classes registered under `officefloor/escalation/`.

Key finding on your intended change: `householdId` does NOT exist yet anywhere in production code. It is referenced only by the target acceptance test (`AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId`), which currently expects owners who opt into `sharesHousehold` to be assigned a shared, non-blank `householdId` readable via `GET /api/owners/{id}`. `sharesHousehold` already exists as a write-only input (openapi + `RejectDuplicateHousehold`), but nothing persists or returns a `householdId`.

## 1. Owner YAML endpoints
Directory: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/`

`owners.POST.yml` (create) — chain:
```
composition: authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
validate  -> RequireOwnerFields          -> normalizeTelephone
normalizeTelephone -> NormalizeOwnerTelephone -> normalizeEmail
normalizeEmail     -> NormalizeOwnerEmail     -> rejectDuplicateTelephone
rejectDuplicateTelephone -> RejectDuplicateTelephone -> rejectDuplicateHousehold
rejectDuplicateHousehold -> RejectDuplicateHousehold -> build
build      -> BuildOwner        (govern: transaction) -> assignCustomerCode
assignCustomerCode -> AssignCustomerCode (transaction) -> save
save       -> SaveOwner         (transaction) -> respond
respond    -> RespondWithOwnerCreated (transaction)
```

`owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` (update) — chain: `ValidateOwner -> NormalizeOwnerEmail -> LoadOwner -> ApplyOwner -> SaveOwner -> RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, all `govern: [ transaction ]`, `authorize hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')`. Note: PUT does NOT run the telephone/duplicate/household chain that POST does.

`owners.GET.yml`: single `ListOwners` (readonly-transaction). `owners/{ownerId}.GET.yml`: `LoadOwner -> RespondWithOwner`. `owners/{ownerId}.DELETE.yml`: `LoadOwner -> DeleteOwner -> common.RespondWithNoContent`.

Other owner-scoped YAMLs exist for pets/visits under `owners/{ownerId}/...` (not detailed; not owner-entity CRUD).

## 2. Owner function classes
Directory: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`

Full contents shown above for all of: `RequireOwnerFields`, `ValidateOwner`, `BuildOwner`, `ApplyOwner`, `LoadOwner`, `SaveOwner`, `AssignCustomerCode`, `NormalizeOwnerEmail`, `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`, `RejectDuplicateHousehold`, `RejectDuplicateTelephone`, `E164Telephone`, `RespondWithOwnerCreated`, `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, `RespondWithOwner`, `DeleteOwner`, `ListOwners`. (Also present: `BuildOwnersPet`, `LoadOwnersPet`, `ListOwnersPage` — for pet sub-resources.)

Most relevant to a household change:
- `RejectDuplicateHousehold.service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerRepository)`: if `sharesHousehold` true, returns early (allows the duplicate); otherwise throws `DuplicateHouseholdException` when an existing owner has the same normalized (trim/collapse-whitespace/lowercase) lastName+address. `normalize()` helper is the household-identity key.
- `BuildOwner.service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerMapper, Out<Owner> built)`: maps DTO->Owner, defaults registrationDate. Publishes `Owner` for downstream steps.
- `AssignCustomerCode`: mutates the published `Owner` in place before save — the natural sibling for where a `householdId` assignment step would slot in (a new function between `build`/`assignCustomerCode` and `save`, publishing/mutating the Owner).
- `SaveOwner`: `ownerRepository.save(owner)`.
- `RespondWithOwnerCreated`/`RespondWithOwner`: map `Owner -> OwnerDto` via `OwnerMapper` for the response, so any returned `householdId` must live on `Owner`+`OwnerDto`+mapper.

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature on `POST /api/owners`, following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

The existing code already had `sharesHousehold` as a write-only input and a `RejectDuplicateHousehold` step that *allowed* a same-lastName + same-address owner when the flag was set, but it never assigned or returned a `householdId`. I added that missing half:

**New behavior** — `AssignHousehold` (`rest/function/owner/AssignHousehold.java`), a transactional step wired into `owners.POST.yml` between `assignCustomerCode` and `save`:
- When `sharesHousehold` is true and an existing owner shares the household (same last name + address, normalized case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace — the same identity key `RejectDuplicateHousehold` uses), it derives a **stable, deterministic** `householdId` (a name-based UUID over the normalized last name + address) and assigns it to the new owner **and** every existing household member (backfilling and saving them within the same transaction, so all members always agree). If the flag is unset or no one shares the household, no id is assigned (stays null).

**Supporting changes to surface/persist the field:**
- `openapi.yml` — added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct auto-maps it onto GET responses).
- `Owner.java` — new `household_id` column + getter/setter.
- `OwnerMapper` — ignore `householdId` when mapping from `OwnerFieldsDto` (consistent with `customerCode`).
- `db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql` — added the `household_id` column.

The acceptance test `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` (owners B and C joining A's household both read back an equal, non-blank `householdId` via `GET /api/owners/{id}`) passes.

One thing worth flagging: `PUT /api/owners/{ownerId}` does **not** run the household chain, so editing an owner's name/address later won't recompute or clear `householdId` — the spec only described the create path, so I scoped it there.
